transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I keep snapping at people. At a safety meeting, I started yelling before I could stop myself. Now the younger inspectors seem scared to come ask me anything.
Have you had times when you felt unusually energized or wired for several days in a row?
I’m not sure what you mean by wired. I haven’t really noticed anything like that for days at a time.
When you snap at people, does it feel like the reaction is much bigger than what set you off?
Yes. It gets bigger than it should. At that safety meeting, I just started yelling before I could stop myself, and it scared the younger inspectors.
When you yell like that, are you trying to get something you want, or does it just burst out before you can stop it?
It just bursts out before I can stop it. I’m not trying to get anything from people—I just start yelling, like I did at that safety meeting.
Has this kind of yelling outburst happened more than once?
Yes, more than once. I keep snapping at people, and it can turn into yelling before I can catch myself. The meeting was the worst one, but it’s happened other times too.
Did these yelling outbursts start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?
I’m not sure I can point to one specific event. I just know I’ve been snapping more, and that meeting made it really obvious. Now the younger inspectors seem scared to even ask me things.
Do these yelling outbursts ever happen when you’ve been drinking alcohol?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether drinking has anything to do with it.
After you have one of these yelling outbursts, do you usually feel sorry or regretful about it?
Yes. Afterward I feel bad about it. I don’t mean to scare people, but I snap and start yelling before I can stop myself.
About how often do these yelling outbursts happen?
It’s been happening a lot lately—often enough that people at work are starting to expect it. Like at that safety meeting, I just start yelling before I can catch myself.
Have these yelling outbursts been happening for at least three months?
Yes, it’s been going on for at least that long. I keep snapping at people, and the younger inspectors are scared to ask me things now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not really sure. I’ve been feeling bad about my outbursts, but I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most days.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah. I’ve pulled back from community theater because I can’t reliably make it through rehearsals anymore. And at work, I’ve missed so many shifts and lost patience with trainees that they don’t trust me to mentor the younger inspectors now.
When you have these yelling outbursts, have you usually been drinking alcohol beforehand?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether drinking beforehand has anything to do with it.
During this same period, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day?
I don’t know that it’s been most of the day, nearly every day. I’ve felt bad about things, but I can’t really say it’s constant like that.
When these yelling outbursts happen, have you been drinking alcohol that day?
I honestly couldn’t tell you. I haven’t paid attention to whether I’d had a drink earlier that day when it happens.
During this period, have you had times when you felt unusually euphoric or intensely irritable for several days in a row?
I’m not really sure what you mean by unusually euphoric. I haven’t noticed several days in a row where I was especially up or intensely irritable.
Have your outbursts ever led you to hit someone or break things?

I haven’t hit anybody or broken anything. It’s more that I snap and start yelling—like at that safety meeting, I was yelling before I could stop myself. Now the younger inspectors seem scared to come ask me things.
Before this started, was there a particular stressful event or major change in your life that happened around the same time?
Yes. It started after that machinery accident, around when we changed to the overnight schedule. That was about two years and four months ago.
Do you have unwanted memories of the machinery accident that keep coming back?
Yes. A clank from a cart, or the smell of hot oil, can put me right back in that bay. I see my coworker by the machine like it’s happening in front of me all over again.
Since the machinery accident, have you been avoiding reminders of it?

Yes. I go out of my way not to pass the inspection bay, and I avoid talking about the accident if I can. I used to go to those industrial-history talks, but I stopped—the pictures of the old machinery set me off.
